crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/compaction.overview: Implements conversation compaction: folding turns that left the history budget into the rolling summary. `run_compaction` is nearly a pure function of transcript and existing summary, and it only writes the new summary after the model output is screened and truncated, so any failure leaves state unchanged. It is the core of the 'Conversation Compaction' step.

sections.title: Limits and errors
sections.explanation: The doc gives the key guarantee: any failure leaves the stored summary untouched, so the next attempt covers the same turns. `FOLD_INPUT_MAX_TOKENS` bounds what is sent to the writer and `SUMMARY_MAX_TOKENS` bounds the stored result. `CompactionError` distinguishes writer failure, empty output and store failure.

sections.title: Summary writer
sections.explanation: `SummaryWriter` abstracts the model so tests can script it. The system prompt asks for neutral third-person notes, drops small talk, excludes sensitive topics and caps length at 150 words. `summary_user_message` formats existing notes, newer messages and an optional focus. `ProviderSummaryWriter` streams a chat from any `AiProvider` and concatenates the deltas.

sections.title: Requester and job types
sections.explanation: `CompactionRequester` lets a tool trigger a compaction on demand, implemented by the app. `CompactionJob` carries the session path, entries, language, limits and focus. `CompactionOutcome` is either `NothingToFold` or the updated summary.

sections.title: Truncation and pending size
sections.explanation: `truncate_to_tokens` keeps whole leading sentences, splitting on CJK and ASCII punctuation, until the budget is reached. `pending_fold_tokens` estimates how many tokens lie between the summary's coverage and the start of the budgeted history; the scheduler compares it to its batch threshold.

sections.title: run_compaction
sections.explanation: Validates the existing summary against the transcript, finds where verbatim history begins using only the budget, and returns `NothingToFold` if already covered. It reads newest-first up to the input cap, so a huge backlog reads its recent part but the summary still advances over all of it. The result is screened for sensitive sentences, truncated and written; an empty result becomes `CompactionError::Empty`.

sections.title: Folded messages
sections.explanation: `folded_messages` recomputes the same newest-first slice the writer saw, so memory extraction examines exactly the turns that were just summarized.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/scheduler..overview: Decides when compaction runs. The decision logic (`decide`) is a pure function of session state and time, which makes it testable with a synthetic clock, while `CompactionScheduler` holds per-session state and spawns runner tasks. Batching, quiet periods, idle and close triggers and exponential backoff keep model calls rare and unobtrusive.

sections.title: Rationale and constants
sections.explanation: The module doc explains why compaction is batched instead of per reply: model cost, CLI quotas and a busy local model. Constants set the 1,200 token batch threshold, 20 second quiet period, 10 minute idle timeout and 60 second to 30 minute backoff range.

sections.title: Config, triggers and state
sections.explanation: `SchedulerConfig` holds the tunables with defaults from the constants. `Trigger` is Batch, Idle or Close. `SessionState` tracks limits, uncovered tokens, last activity, in-flight flags, failure count, and pending close and idle flags.

sections.title: Backoff and decide
sections.explanation: `backoff` doubles the delay per failure, capped at 16 doublings and the maximum. `decide` returns nothing while a reply or compaction is running, when nothing is uncovered, or during backoff. Then close beats idle, and idle beats batch, which requires both enough tokens and a quiet period.

sections.title: Clock and runner abstractions
sections.explanation: `Clock` is injectable so tests control time. `CompactionRunner` performs one compaction and returns remaining unsummarized tokens. `CompactionScheduler` keeps a mutex-protected map of session paths to state.

sections.title: Note methods
sections.explanation: `update` is a short-lock helper that creates state on demand. `note_reply_started` records the limits the request used and blocks compaction while the reply streams. `note_reply_finished` records uncovered tokens. `note_limits` handles a request trimmed further by the fit check. `note_window_closed` and `request_now` both set `close_pending`.

sections.title: Tick
sections.explanation: `tick` locks the map, marks due sessions in flight and collects them, then releases the lock before spawning tasks. On success a task stores remaining tokens and clears failures; on error it increments the failure count and timestamp so `decide` applies backoff. Returned join handles exist for tests.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/summary.rs.overview: Defines the rolling `ConversationSummary` and where it lives. The summary is kept in a sidecar JSON file beside the session, so the transcript stays untouched and a missing or corrupt file simply means no summary.

sections.title: Why a sidecar
sections.explanation: The module doc justifies the design: no new log role, no UI changes, safe failure state. The summary is restartable because it only claims to cover the first `covered_through` context-visible messages.

sections.title: ConversationSummary and matches
sections.explanation: The struct stores coverage count, text, update time and the timestamp of the last covered message. `matches` rejects a summary that claims more messages than exist or whose last covered timestamp no longer lines up, detecting an edited or replaced log. A missing timestamp (older files) is trusted.

sections.title: SummaryStore trait and path
sections.explanation: The trait abstracts reading and writing so compaction tests need no filesystem. `summary_path` appends `.summary.json` to the session file name; the `.json` extension keeps session listing, which looks for `.jsonl`, from treating it as a conversation.

sections.title: File-backed store
sections.explanation: `read` swallows IO and parse errors into `None`. `write` creates the parent directory, writes to a `.tmp` file and renames it into place, so a crash leaves either the old summary or none, never a partial file.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/ext.overview: After a compaction, asks the background model to propose durable memories from the turns just folded. It only proposes: candidates are screened and saved as automatic memories and never replace existing ones.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.explanation: The doc says extraction runs once per compaction on the same background model and goes through the sensitive-topic screen and write policy. A budget limits how many known facts are shown to the model.

sections.title: extract_after_compaction
sections.explanation: `transcript` keeps only user and assistant messages. The function returns 0 for an empty transcript, lists known facts so the model avoids repeats, asks the model to complete, parses candidates and saves them with a source tag and persona name. Errors are returned as strings for the caller to log, since compaction has already succeeded.

sections.title: Known facts
sections.explanation: `known_facts` uses the same ranking digest on local-audience active memories, with a fallback text when the store is empty.

crates/fleet-snowfluff/src/compaction_ru.overview: The app-side glue for compaction. It builds the real `CompactionRunner` and `CompactionRequester`, runs a ticker that polls the scheduler every 5 seconds, and exposes small hooks the chat code calls when replies start and finish or the window closes. Everything is best effort and off the reply path.

sections.title: Overview and imports
sections.explanation: The doc promises that compaction never delays a reply and that unrunnable cases are skipped silently, since the transcript on disk is unchanged. `TICK_INTERVAL` sets the 5 second poll.

sections.title: compact_session
sections.explanation: Reads AI settings and credentials, then bails with `Ok(None)` if AI is off, there is no background profile, or the cloud disclosure is unacknowledged. Otherwise it reads the session, records the summary coverage before, builds a fresh provider (CLI profiles get a throwaway session) and runs `run_compaction`. On an update it kicks off memory extraction.

sections.title: Memory extraction after compaction
sections.explanation: `extract_memories` runs only if memory is enabled and something was folded. It builds a source label from the file name and covered range, then spawns a background task that runs extraction and notifies the UI if anything was stored. Failures are only debug-logged.

sections.title: Runner and requester
sections.explanation: `AppCompactionRunner` implements `CompactionRunner`, mapping outcomes to remaining pending tokens and returning 0 when it cannot run to avoid pointless retries. `AppCompactionRequester` serves the on-demand tool, using the scheduler's last limits and focus, and turns 'no model' into an error.

sections.title: Scheduler startup and hooks
sections.explanation: `start` creates the scheduler, registers it as managed Tauri state and spawns the loop that calls `tick`. The hook functions (`reply_started`, `history_was_trimmed`, `reply_finished_for`, `reply_finished`, `window_closed`) look up the scheduler and forward state. `history_was_trimmed` sets a budget of the tokens actually kept so later compaction covers what was dropped.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/protoc.overview: The transport-independent MCP client protocol: the `initialize` handshake, `tools/list` and `tools/call`, over any `McpTransport`. It also defines the wire types and converts a tool-call result into the agent's `ToolResult`.

sections.title: Version and identity
sections.explanation: The doc notes the calls are the same for all compliant servers regardless of transport. A fixed protocol version `2025-06-18` is sent and the server is trusted to negotiate down. `client_info` supplies the name and crate version.

sections.title: Wire types and result conversion
sections.explanation: `McpToolDescriptor` mirrors a `tools/list` entry, with `inputSchema` renamed. `McpContentBlock` is tagged by `type` with a catch-all `Other` so unknown block types do not fail the call. `McpToolCallResult::into_tool_result` joins text blocks and maps `isError` to `ToolResult::error`, keeping tool-level failures distinct from JSON-RPC errors.

sections.title: McpClient
sections.explanation: `McpClient` is a thin clone-able wrapper over an `Arc<dyn McpTransport>`. `initialize` sends the request then the `notifications/initialized` notification; ordering before other calls is a convention, not enforced by types. `list_tools` tolerates a missing `tools` field, and `call_tool` serializes name and arguments, with deserialization errors mapped to `McpError`.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/transp.overview: Defines the McpTransport trait, the single seam between MCP protocol logic (McpClient) and however a server is reached. It lets McpClient be written once while stdio and HTTP/SSE transports plug in behind it. It is the abstraction the MCP Client tour step builds on.

sections.title: Design rationale
sections.explanation: The module docs explain why the trait works at request/response level rather than raw bytes. Matching a response to its request id is a transport concern: stdio must correlate lines on a shared stream, while HTTP gets pairing for free. Keeping that out of McpClient avoids duplicating bookkeeping in every transport.

sections.title: McpTransport trait
sections.explanation: An async trait with two methods matching JSON-RPC 2.0's message shapes: `request` returns the `result` value or an McpError, and `notify` is fire-and-forget. `Send + Sync` lets an `Arc<dyn McpTransport>` be shared across tasks, and `async_trait` makes the async methods object-safe.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/stdio_.overview: Implements McpTransport over a spawned subprocess's stdin/stdout using newline-delimited JSON-RPC, as MCP's stdio spec defines. It handles process lifetime (kill on drop) and request/response id matching. The tests run a real Python fixture server and verify that dropping the transport kills the child.

sections.title: Module docs and imports
sections.explanation: The docs state two key decisions: `kill_on_drop(true)` so an abandoned connection never leaves a server running, and one in-flight request per connection. The single-request limit is justified because every MCP tool is Confirm-tier and the agent runtime executes those serially.

sections.title: JSON-RPC response types
sections.explanation: Minimal serde structs for decoding a server line. Every field is `#[serde(default)]` and optional, so notifications (no id) or responses with only `result` or only `error` all deserialize without failing.

sections.title: Struct and spawn
sections.explanation: `StdioTransport` keeps the child, stdin and a line reader each behind a tokio `Mutex`, plus an atomic id counter. `spawn` pipes stdin/stdout, discards stderr, sets `kill_on_drop`, and returns before any MCP handshake. The `_child` field is held only so dropping it terminates the process.

sections.title: Writing a line
sections.explanation: Serializes a JSON value, appends a newline, then writes and flushes under the stdin lock. Flushing is required because the server will not see a partial buffered line.

sections.title: Request and notify
sections.explanation: `request` takes a fresh id from the atomic counter, writes the call, then holds the reader lock and loops until a line whose `id` matches arrives, skipping blank lines, notifications and foreign ids. A JSON-RPC `error` becomes an McpError that includes its code, and EOF becomes a 'server closed the connection' error. `notify` omits the id and reads nothing back.

sections.title: Tests with a real subprocess
sections.explanation: Unix-only tests. The first writes a tiny Python script acting as an MCP server and round-trips `initialize` and `tools/list` through McpClient, skipping if Python is missing. The second spawns `cat` and polls `ps` to prove that dropping the transport terminates the child.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/oauth..overview: The OAuth 2.1 building blocks for HTTP MCP servers: discovery via 401 and WWW-Authenticate, Dynamic Client Registration, PKCE, token exchange and refresh, and a one-shot loopback redirect listener. It deliberately does not open a browser, since this crate has no tauri dependency. The app crate opens the URL this module builds.

sections.title: Scope and imports
sections.explanation: The docs map each OAuth feature to its function and explain the crate boundary. This crate decides what should happen and the app crate launches the browser, the same split used by the agent's streaming callback.

sections.title: Authorization probe
sections.explanation: Sends one unauthenticated `initialize` and classifies the result as NotRequired or Required (carrying the WWW-Authenticate header). Other failures propagate as errors instead of being mistaken for either outcome.

sections.title: PKCE, state and URL building
sections.explanation: Generates a random 32-byte verifier, its SHA-256 S256 challenge, and a random `state` value used for CSRF protection. `build_authorization_url` percent-encodes every parameter and includes the `resource` parameter (RFC 8707) to bind the token to one MCP server. The redirect wait is capped at 300 seconds.

sections.title: Discovery
sections.explanation: Two hops: the protected-resource metadata (URL taken from the `resource_metadata` header parameter, or the well-known path on the server's origin as a fallback), then the first listed authorization server's own metadata. Only the endpoints this client needs are deserialized.

sections.title: Dynamic client registration
sections.explanation: Registers a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`) with a loopback redirect URI. If the server advertises no registration endpoint, the wrapper returns a clear error naming the server rather than failing obscurely.

sections.title: Token exchange and refresh
sections.explanation: Posts form-encoded grant requests to the token endpoint. The code exchange sends the PKCE verifier, and a manually pasted code takes the same path as one caught by the listener. Refresh returns a new TokenResponse whose refresh token may rotate.

sections.title: Redirect parsing helpers
sections.explanation: Hand-written percent decoding and request-line parsing keep the loopback listener dependency-free. The query is read from the first HTTP line only, read byte by byte until a newline.

sections.title: RedirectListener
sections.explanation: Binds to 127.0.0.1 on an OS-chosen port, answers exactly one request with a 'you can close this tab' page, and consumes `self`. It returns the code only if `state` matches the expected value, so forged or stale redirects are rejected. The whole wait is wrapped in a timeout.

sections.title: Tests
sections.explanation: Cover PKCE correctness, URL encoding, the probe, both discovery hops against mocked servers, registration, token exchange and refresh, and the listener's success and state-mismatch paths.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/tool.r.overview: Adapts one discovered MCP tool to the agent's native Tool trait, so the agent loop cannot tell it apart from a built-in tool. It always requires user confirmation and never offers 'remember for this session'. This is the final step of the MCP Client tour stop, connecting it back to the agent runtime.

sections.title: McpTool struct
sections.explanation: Holds a tool descriptor plus an McpClient handle. The client is cheap to clone because it wraps an Arc'd transport, so a server's whole tool list shares one connection.

sections.title: Tool trait implementation
sections.explanation: `definition` maps the discovered name, description (empty if absent) and JSON input schema into a ToolDefinition. `required_permission` is always Confirm and `allows_session_remember` is always false, because MCP carries no risk metadata. `execute` calls `tools/call` and converts the result or error into the agent's ToolResult or ToolError.

sections.title: Unit tests
sections.explanation: Use a ScriptedTransport test double to verify schema translation, the empty-description fallback, the fixed permission behavior, and both success and transport-failure execution paths.

ui/src/main.ts.overview: The single TypeScript entry point for every Tauri webview window. At startup it branches on the window label to render the chat window, status bubble, tool-confirmation popup, or the tabbed settings UI. It talks to the Rust backend through `invoke` and events, and uses an embedded dictionary for localization.

sections.title: Imports and shared types
sections.explanation: Imports Tauri APIs and Pico.css, then declares TypeScript mirrors of the Rust-side data: config, AI provider profiles, memory records, MCP server records, and chat and confirmation payloads. These types are the contract for `invoke` calls.

sections.title: Localization helper
sections.explanation: `t()` looks up a key in a dictionary loaded once via the `locale_dictionary` command, falls back to the key itself, and substitutes `{name}` placeholders. Translation is resolved on the Rust side, so the frontend only holds one flat dictionary.

sections.title: State and window opacity
sections.explanation: Tracks the active settings tab and any update found by the startup check. Window opacity is fetched once and kept in sync by an `opacity-changed` event instead of polling, and is applied to `#app` as an inline style.

sections.title: Entry dispatch (main)
sections.explanation: All windows share one index.html, so `main` branches on `getCurrentWindow().label` for chat, status-bubble and tool-confirmation. The settings path loads the dictionary, renders, and registers listeners for tab switches, MCP server changes (from a detached OAuth task) and memory changes. A failure paints an error rather than leaving a blank window.

sections.title: Settings shell and tabs
sections.explanation: `render` builds the tab strip and four panels, then fills each with `Promise.allSettled` so one failing panel shows its own error without blocking others. Opening the AI tab refreshes only provider status, which avoids discarding unsaved edits.

sections.title: Personalization and AI panels
sections.explanation: `renderPersonalization` builds the settings form, and `renderAi` and `renderAiPanel` build the provider, router, MCP and memory sections as HTML strings with event wiring afterward.

sections.title: Memory and MCP management
sections.explanation: Renders the long-term memory list (search, edit, history rows) and refreshes only the list when `memories-changed` fires, so typing is not lost. The MCP section lists servers and their tools and provides add and connect forms, including the OAuth code-submission flow.

sections.title: Provider profiles, update and about tabs
sections.explanation: Each provider and auth-method slot gets a collapsible row with save, login and live status checks. The update tab reuses the startup result and can check GitHub on demand, and the about tab shows version and external links.

sections.title: Status bubble window
sections.explanation: A tiny window that polls `get_chat_state` every 500 ms and shows a fixed glyph: '...' while pending, a happy face after an assistant reply, and a failure face after an error. It reuses the chat snapshot instead of adding bubble-specific IPC.

sections.title: Chat and tool-confirmation windows
sections.explanation: `mainChat` renders the transcript, input form and conversation list. The tool-confirmation popup builds DOM nodes (not HTML strings) per pending tool call, with approve-all and deny-all, an optional remember checkbox, and submits via `resolve_tool_confirmations`, then fetches the next batch. The file ends by calling `main()`.

ui/src/style.css.overview: Small stylesheet layered on Pico.css for the Fleet Snowfluff windows. It sets a fixed pink theme by overriding Pico variables, loads the pixel font, and styles the settings tabs, chat, confirmation popup, status bubble, and AI and memory sections.

sections.title: Font and fallback chain
sections.explanation: Declares the zpix pixel font and puts it first in Pico's `--pico-font-family`, with Noto fonts as fallbacks. The comment notes zpix has no Hangul glyphs, so the fallbacks keep Korean from rendering as tofu boxes.

sections.title: Fixed pink theme
sections.explanation: Overrides Pico's color variables with a pink-and-white palette regardless of OS theme. Each value uses `!important` because Pico's `:root:not([data-theme=dark])` selector is more specific than a plain `:root`.

sections.title: Transparent window base
sections.explanation: Makes html and body transparent and puts the background on `#app`, so the opacity set by main.ts fades the background together with the content and the desktop shows through.

sections.title: Settings tabs and rows
sections.explanation: Flex column layout for the settings window, the tab strip, active-panel toggling, compact label-left rows, about-panel styling, and error and hint text.

sections.title: Chat window
sections.explanation: Styles the transcript and its user, assistant, pending and error entries, the input form, and the conversation list with its open and delete buttons.

sections.title: Confirmation popup and bubble
sections.explanation: Layout for the tool-confirmation items and actions, plus the status bubble, which gets its own `#app` treatment on the bubble window body.

sections.title: AI, MCP and memory sections
sections.explanation: Styles AI fieldsets, per-profile details rows with an experimental badge and connection status colors, the MCP server and tool lists, and the memory rows and badges.

ui/vite.config.ts.overview: Minimal Vite configuration for the Tauri frontend. It fixes the dev server port so tauri.conf.json's devUrl always matches, and keeps Vite from watching Rust sources.

sections.title: Vite config for Tauri
sections.explanation: `clearScreen: false` keeps Rust compiler output visible. Port 1420 with `strictPort` makes Vite fail rather than pick another port, since Tauri expects exactly that URL. The watcher ignores `**/crates/**` so Rust edits do not trigger frontend reloads.

crates/fleet-snowfluff/tauri.conf.json.overview: Tauri's main configuration for the desktop app: product identity, how the frontend is built and served, bundle targets, signing, and the auto-updater. The window list is empty because windows are created in Rust code.

sections.title: Identity and build hooks
sections.explanation: Names the product and points `frontendDist` at ui/dist and `devUrl` at the Vite server on port 1420. The before-dev and before-build commands run npm scripts in the ui folder.

sections.title: macOS dylib fix hook
sections.explanation: The `beforeBundleCommand` runs a repo script to fix dylib paths, but only on Darwin. Other platforms exit immediately.

sections.title: App and security
sections.explanation: Enables the macOS private API (needed for transparent windows) and declares no static windows, because pet and chat windows are created at runtime. The CSP is set to null, so no content security policy is applied.

sections.title: Bundling
sections.explanation: Builds NSIS, deb, AppImage, dmg and app targets, produces updater artifacts, lists icons, and signs the macOS build with a self-signed identity.

sections.title: Updater plugin
sections.explanation: Points the updater at the GitHub releases `latest.json` and embeds the public key used to verify update signatures.

crates/fleet-snowfluff/capabilities/defa.overview: The Tauri capability file that grants webview windows their permissions. It follows least privilege by naming only the windows that need access and a short list of permissions.

sections.title: Default capability
sections.explanation: Applies to the settings, chat, status-bubble windows and any `pet-*` window (glob). It grants `core:default`, `shell:allow-open` (used by the UI to open external links) and `dialog:default` (folder picker and confirm dialogs). Note the tool-confirmation window label that main.ts handles is not listed here.

Provider that drives the Claude Code CLI as a subprocess with stream-json parsing, session resume, history seeding, tool allow/deny args and login checks; heavily tested with fake CLIs.
Carries per-request context (history and seen-turn state) for CLI-backed providers.
Locates CLI executables via cached PATH search, platform fallback directories, Windows registry and login-shell PATH extraction.
Shared helpers for spawning CLI chat processes: spawn settings, error mapping and liveness checks.
Provider driving the Codex CLI as a subprocess with JSON line parsing, temp instruction files, session resume and error classification.
Renders conversation history into a budgeted text preamble for CLI sessions that lack native history, with resume-aware turn selection.
Shared HTTP streaming helpers that turn response bodies into line streams, with single, multi and stateful parser variants.
Buffers byte chunks and yields complete lines, reassembling lines split across chunks.
Mock provider that echoes the last user message in multiple chunks for offline use and tests.
Module declaration file wiring all provider implementations and shared helpers.
Ollama local provider using NDJSON chat streaming, tool-calling, model listing and loaded-context-window detection with caching.
OpenAI-compatible provider with chat and tool-call request building, SSE parsing and a streaming tool-call parser that reassembles fragmented arguments.
Tiny in-process HTTP server for tests that captures a request and serves a canned response.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/context_bu.overview: Resolves a model name to its context window and provides the in-run safety net that replaces the oldest tool results when a long agent run fills the window.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/credential.overview: Serde shape of secrets.json holding provider API keys and per-MCP-server credentials, kept apart from AiSettings so config files never contain secrets.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/execution..overview: Persisted Execution records (start/end events, route, status, tool invocations) with JSONL serialization, parsing and pairing of events into executions.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/fit.rs.overview: Pre-flight fit check that sheds optional request parts (history, summary, memory, few-shot, tool stubs) in order to fit the context window without ever trimming the persona prompt.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/lib.rs.overview: Crate root of fleet-snowfluff-ai declaring all modules and re-exporting the public API (agent runtime, providers, MCP, memory, compaction, scheduler, settings); the crate stays independent of core and the app crate.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/limits.rs.overview: Fixed Stage 1 cost/latency constants: history token budget, window percentage, uncovered extra tokens, max history messages and max response tokens, with a note on why no Ollama num_ctx is set.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/log.rs.overview: Session log entry format (JSONL) with serialize/parse functions and conversion of visible entries into context messages.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/persona.rs.overview: Persona file model and all-or-nothing YAML parsing, with fallback to the bundled default persona and a surfaced parse-failure reason.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/sensitive..overview: Deterministic keyword screen for sensitive topics (health, money, credentials, sexuality, religion, politics) used to strip sentences from summaries and memory extraction output.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/bac.overview: Background memory writers that run after an assistant reply: a remember-cue backstop that saves facts the model failed to store via tool, a correction handler that supersedes memories, and an LLM extraction pass with sensitive-topic filtering. Includes multilingual cue detection and tests.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/fak.overview: In-memory fake implementation of the memory service used in tests, validated against the shared behavior suite.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/mod.overview: Module root for the memory subsystem defining core types (Audience, Origin, Kind, Status, MemoryRecord, NewMemory, MemoryEdit) and the MemoryService trait, and wiring together the store, policy, rank, tokenizer and block submodules.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/pol.overview: Save policy for new memories: dedupes by normalized text, applies supersede-on-correction rules, drops derived memories about sensitive topics, and rejects blank text.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/sui.overview: Shared behavior test suite run against every MemoryService implementation to guarantee consistent semantics for add, search, supersede, forget, edit and audience filtering.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/memory/tok.overview: Multilingual tokenizer for memory indexing and search that folds traditional to simplified Chinese, normalizes full-width text, and produces CJK bigrams, stopword-filtered Latin tokens and single-character fallbacks.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/token_esti.overview: Heuristic token estimator weighting characters by class (CJK, structured text, prose) calibrated to never undershoot measured counts, with helpers for messages and tool definitions.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/tool_outpu.overview: Bounds oversize tool outputs by estimated tokens, spilling the remainder to size-capped part files in a spill directory with a visible truncation marker, and prunes old spill files.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/config.overview: Serde models for persisted MCP server configuration: transports, status, cached tools, disabled tools and JSON load/serialize helpers.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/error..overview: Defines the McpError error type shared by MCP transports and client code.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/http_t.overview: HTTP transport for MCP that sends JSON-RPC requests and notifications with bearer auth, error mapping and timeouts, with mock-server tests.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/mcp/mod.rs.overview: Module root for the MCP client subsystem declaring config, error, transports, OAuth, protocol and tool submodules.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-core/src/voice.rs.overview: Voice-language enum, clip manifest schema, snap-back rule to a language with clips, and a clip selector that avoids long repeats.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/conversati.overview: Defines ConversationId, a newtype identifying a conversation by its session log file path, shared by the agent tool context without depending on the app crate.

crates/fleet-snowfluff-ai/src/native_too.overview: Module wiring that declares the native tool submodules offered to the tool-calling agent.
Implements the compact_context tool that lets the assistant request summarization of older conversation, with an optional focus hint, using a CompactionRequester; withheld from child agents.

Provides read_file and list_directory tools with a byte cap on reads, UTF-8-safe truncation, project-root path containment checks (symlink and dot-dot aware), and auto-approval for spilled output files.
Defines four memory tools (search, get, remember, forget) over MemoryService, with read tools available to child agents and write tools restricted, plus privacy handling for sensitive entries.
Implements get_system_context, reporting OS, time, CPU and memory stats via sysinfo, deliberately excluding window title, idle time and clipboard.
Implements web_search with a three-tier no-key fallback (local ddgs server, public SearXNG, DuckDuckGo Instant Answer), a ddgs cooldown cache, an injectable transport and extensive parser tests.
